title: H206 Halloween Effect — Regulatory Disclosure Mechanism Strengthens Hypothesis
summary: A November 2025 paper (Schroeder, TU Dortmund, IJFS) identifies SEC regulatory disclosure seasonality as a novel mechanism for the Halloween effect. From 2004-2023: SEC filings 17% higher in winter (Nov-Apr) vs summer (May-Oct); February highest, September lowest. Winter also has 22% more insider trading, 473% more annual reports, 96% more shareholder meetings. This provides a concrete information-flow mechanism for the Halloween premium that complements the existing vacation/attention explanations — more value-relevant information arrives in winter, higher market efficiency and price discovery, potentially lower risk. For H206 design (hold SPY in Nov-Apr, hold BIL in May-Oct), this is positive: the anomaly has a structural information-based driver that is unlikely to be easily arbitraged (it reflects real corporate calendar rhythms tied to fiscal year ends and regulatory cycles). Confirms H206 as a viable candidate with fundamentally sound underpinning. Note: recent data (2010-2024) shows reduced edge (~2.8%/yr annualized), so H206 success depends on whether TOM composite boosts the signal.
